speaker: Doctor
text: I see you're experiencing fatigue, flank pain, and fever following recent antibiotic treatment for acute sinusitis. To help me understand your condition better, have you noticed any changes in your urine, such as frequency, urgency, or unusual appearance?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling tired, feverish, and I have flank pain. These symptoms continued even after my sinus symptoms improved.

speaker: Doctor
text: The fever and flank pain persisting after your sinus infection suggests the infection may have spread; have you noticed any burning sensation when you urinate or passed any blood? REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis

text: RESULTS: Urinalysis: Leukocyturia: Present; Bacterial_Culture: Negative; Cytospin_Stained_With_Hansel’s_Solution: 3% binucleated cells with eosinophilic, granular cytoplasm

speaker: Doctor
text: The urinalysis shows white blood cells but no bacteria, and the cytospin reveals eosinophilic granular cells, which is highly suggestive of an allergic interstitial reaction rather than a bacterial infection. Given your recent antibiotic use for sinusitis, have you noticed any rash, itching, or swelling of your lips or tongue? REQUEST IMAGES: Renal_ultrasound

speaker: Patient
text: I was first treated with amoxicillin for sinusitis and developed a rash. Then the antibiotic was changed to cephalexin for another week, and the rash went away.

speaker: Doctor
text: The timeline of the rash appearing with amoxicillin and resolving after switching to cephalexin, combined with eosinophilic cells in your urine, strongly suggests acute interstitial nephritis. Have you been experiencing nausea, vomiting, or a decreased urine output recently? REQUEST IMAGES: Renal_ultrasound

speaker: Patient
text: I do not have nausea, vomiting, or burning with urination. I also have not noticed a major change in urine color.

speaker: Doctor
text: That confirms the absence of typical urinary tract symptoms, supporting our suspicion of an allergic reaction. To confirm the diagnosis of Acute Interstitial Nephritis, I need to see your kidney imaging and check your kidney function levels. REQUEST IMAGES: Renal_ultrasound, REQUEST TEST: Serum_Creatinine

speaker: Doctor
text:
The elevated serum creatinine confirms impaired kidney function, and combined with the eosinophilic cells in your urine and the rash after amoxicillin, this is highly suggestive of Acute Interstitial Nephritis. Since we have gathered sufficient evidence from your history, lab results, and the lack of other urinary symptoms, I am ready to finalize my assessment.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Interstitial Nephritis
